Informed consent

A process that requires:
▘ Disclosure: discussion of pertinent
information, including risks/benefits
▘ Understanding: ability to comprehend
▘ Capacity: ability to reason and make one’s
own decisions (distinct from competence, a
legal determination)
▘ Voluntariness: freedom from coercion and
manipulation

kypExtensions.summary: The four-question router that turns the page's three blocks into one decision procedure: (1) WHO is the decider — adult with capacity, minor, or capacity lost; (2) does the PROCESS stand — the four printed requirements run in order (Disclosure with the alternatives-and-no-treatment set, Understanding, Capacity, Voluntariness) with the revocation clause attached; (3) is the patient a MINOR — run the gates (emergency treatment, emancipation, the Sex/Drugs/Rock-and-roll set) with assent and minor-guardian communication on every path; (4) if capacity is LOST — match the instrument (oral directive, living will, medical power of attorney, DNR scope).
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the three blocks as parallel doctrine; the single router that sequences them (decider → process → exception → substitute) is KYP's organization.
kypExtensions.location: core.keyIdea MOVES 1-4 + mechanisms[0] and [1] + blocks[3] the steps block + the registry visual's four zones

kypExtensions.summary: The reading of the WIPE exceptions as the four ways the consent process fails, each with its guardrail: Waiver = the patient explicitly relinquishes the process (a family's request is never a waiver); Legally Incompetent = the capacity pillar is absent and consent routes to the legal surrogate (capacity clinical vs competence legal); Therapeutic Privilege = the physician withholds, and only when disclosure would severely harm the patient or undermine informed decision-making capacity; Emergency = implied consent may apply, and lasts only as long as the emergency. The capacity-vs-competence clinical/legal gloss and the guardrails beyond the printed conditions are KYP's.
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the four exceptions as a list; mapping each onto a process failure point and adding the guardrails is KYP's synthesis.
kypExtensions.location: mechanisms[0] the WIPE node and its edges + blocks[2] decoder WIPE item + blocks[4] exam callout SHAPE 1 + usmle.traps[0-1]

kypExtensions.summary: The advance-directive flexibility ladder — WORDS (oral directive: prior statements, problems from variance in interpretation, strengthened by the four printed validity boosters) → PAPER (written directive / living will: specific interventions for critical or life-threatening illness, rigid but precise) → PERSON (medical power of attorney: a designated agent, printed 'more flexible than a living will', revocable while capacity is intact) — with the DNR order drawn BESIDE the ladder as the scoped order that prohibits CPR only (intubation, feeding tube, chemotherapy remain separate decisions). The full ladder ordering is the KYP synthesis of the printed cues; the print ranks only implicitly.
kypExtensions.rationale: The source's only explicit ranking language is 'More flexible than a living will' (POA row) plus the Oral row's interpretation problems; assembling the three-rung ladder and placing the DNR outside it is KYP's synthesis, flagged as such on the visual, in the note, and here.
kypExtensions.location: mechanisms[1] the ladder node + blocks[2] decoder ladder item + blocks[5] the living-will-vs-POA compare block + the registry visual's Zone D

kypExtensions.summary: The pattern/trap/pivot/mini-case attack structure layered over the printed page — 4 patterns (the therapeutic-privilege-limit stem, the 15-year-old contraception stem, the DNR-scope intubation stem, the living-will-vs-POA flexibility stem), 4 traps (capacity vs competence; waiver vs therapeutic privilege; emancipation vs the Sex/Drugs/Rock-and-roll set; DNR vs withdrawal of life-sustaining measures), 3 pivots (the signed-form tell, the minor-gates router, the instrument matcher), and 8 recall cards covering every printed block.
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid prints the doctrine only; the attack structure, distractor designs, and question shapes are KYP's design.
